summary: Typosquat package ships a Telegram-controlled remote command executor loaded on import
details: Package name 'httpz-requests' resembles the popular 'requests' / 'httpx' HTTP clients, but the distribution metadata declares Summary 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management' and requires python-telegram-bot>=20.0. The top-level __init__.py re-exports start_bot from a bundled bot module (from.bot import start_bot), so a plain `import httpz_requests` starts a Telegram-bot-driven command executor that lets a remote party holding the bot token/chat ID run commands on the installer's host. All modules (bot, core, handlers, cli, constants, obfuscate) ship only as Cython-compiled.so binaries with no Python source and were built with string-table compression (CYTHON_COMPRESS_STRINGS, __Pyx_DecompressString), concealing the hardcoded bot token, chat ID, and command handlers from inspection. Publisher metadata is unfilled template values (Author-email 'Aapka Naam <you@example.com>', Homepage 'https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests'), consistent with a throwaway identity. The combination of name/functionality mismatch, import-time backdoor startup, compiled-only payload, and placeholder publisher metadata is a targeted attack on developers searching for HTTP client libraries.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
